title: Aggregate earnings-announcement premium: hold the Nasdaq 100 CFD long Monday-to-Friday only in the weeks when most S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 companies report (weeks 2 to 6 after each quarter-end), with every other week of the year as the control arm; replication on the S&P 500 and Nikkei 225 CFDs
rationale: Mechanism: a risk premium, not a flow. Earnings news is systematic information; investors who hold the index through the weeks when most companies report bear concentrated cash-flow and discount-rate news and may be paid for it on average, as Savor and Wilson (2013) show for scheduled macro-announcement days (where the market's excess return is concentrated) and as Savor and Wilson (2016) and Barber, De George, Lehavy and Trueman (2013) show at the firm level for announcers against non-announcers. The firm-level spread cancels in a cap-weighted index, so neither paper gives an index-level size; this test asks whether any index-level excess exists in reporting weeks, and the honest prior is small: 0 to +0.1 percent a week (0 to +0.08 R at a 1.0 x ATR20 stop). Reporting is concentrated by the calendar: large US companies report from about the second week after a quarter-end for four to five weeks; Tokyo companies with a March year-end about two weeks later. The programme has never conditioned an index hold on the reporting calendar; its index work tested calendar flows (turn-of-month, option expiry, pension rebalancing), overnight and pre-holiday drift, intraday momentum, FOMC drift, dip-buying and vol timing. The charter's warning that long-only index tests pass by luck is met inside the design: the control arm is long in every non-season week of the same years, so drift, costs and financing are identical in both arms and only the reporting-week excess is scored, paired by calendar quarter. Confound stated up front: every season window contains the first-month-of-quarter FOMC meeting (about 20-22 percent of season weeks hold a decision against about 12 percent of control weeks) and prior_fomc_cycle found a pre-FOMC drift since 2016, so the difference is also reported with FOMC weeks dropped from both arms and the hypothesis is scrapped if that difference is not positive in design. Design: H1 bars on the Nasdaq 100 CFD (USATECHIDXUSD) from 2013 (2011 has six days of data; 2012 bars carry no spread), one trade per week, long at the open of the 15:00 UTC Monday bar, exit at the open of the 20:00 UTC Friday bar (the last bar of the Friday session in US daylight time), stop 1.0 or 2.0 x ATR20, no target, with a causal fallback exit over the weekend gap. Season weeks are fixed from the calendar before any data is seen (Monday start_off = 10 or 17 days after the quarter start, n_weeks = 4 or 5), bracketing the reporting calendar without reading it from the data. Counts (design 2013-2017, from the calendar and the bar census, no outcomes): about 70-90 season weeks and 140-170 control weeks per cell; check 2018-2023 similar; USA500IDXUSD from 2013, JPNIDXJPY from 2014 (about 60-70 design season weeks) with the 14-day shift. Costs (engine index costs: raw spread, 1 point of slippage per fill, financing per night with Wednesday tripled, so 6 nights for a Monday-to-Friday hold): about 0.15-0.25 percent of the index per week in 2013-2014, less later; a 1.0 x ATR20 stop is about 1.5-2 percent of the index, so about 0.10-0.13 R at sl 1.0 and 0.05-0.07 R at sl 2.0. Expected: the control near 0 to +0.05 R in design (the earlier non-opex weekly Nasdaq long, index_flows C1, made -0.019 R in design and +0.067 R in check); the season arm 0 to +0.08 R above it. Power is low: with about 85 season and 165 control weeks the standard error of the difference is about 0.14 R, so P(design paired-D t >= 1 | effect real at +0.05 to +0.08 R) is about 0.25-0.35 and about 0.16 if there is no effect; a kill is weak evidence, a pass is modest evidence, and the pass bar (design t >= 2) is reachable only if the effect is much larger than the prior. The most likely outcome is an inconclusive negative, which still records that the reporting calendar carries no weekly-hold excess large enough to trade on a CFD. Human execution: one order a week for about 16-20 weeks a year, Monday morning New York, Friday afternoon exit; executable on a prop account that allows index CFDs.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on USATECHIDXUSD, applied by the Director from all 16 stage A rows in the trials table (stage 'A') even if the pipeline reports a candidate (the automatic stage A gate ranks all 16 cells by design t, so a control cell can clear it): among the 8 season cells with at least 60 design trades, the chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t (the pipeline's own ranking); it must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and season-window-clustered t >= 1 (R averaged per calendar quarter of the entry date, then t over those quarter means); otherwise scrap. If the automatic floor is cleared only by a ctrl cell, the B/C output is ignored and the hypothesis is scrapped under this rule. (2) Quarter-paired control difference, the only drift-neutral test and the one promotion depends on: for the chosen cell and its matching ctrl cell (same start_off, n_weeks and sl_atr), D_q = mean R of the season weeks in calendar quarter q minus mean R of the non-season weeks in the same quarter, over quarters with at least one week in each arm; require mean D > 0 with t(D over quarters) >= 1.0 in design, and mean D > 0 in check. If promoted, the locked holdout run also runs the matching ctrl cell (same touch, counted) and the holdout requires chosen minus matching ctrl > 0; a holdout where that difference is <= 0 is a fail even if the raw holdout avg R > 0. (3) FOMC attribution: report D in design and in check after dropping, from both arms, every week that contains a scheduled FOMC decision (dates from the 'Federal Funds Rate' rows of data/external/calendar_spoluan/forex_factory_calendar_YYYY.csv, stamped about 8 hours ahead of UTC); if the design D excluding FOMC weeks is <= 0, scrap with the lesson that the season excess is the pre-FOMC drift already measured in prior_fomc_cycle. (4) Breadth: at the chosen cell, at least 3 of the 4 reporting seasons (January, April, July, October) must have a positive design D, and design avg R must stay > 0 after dropping the best ceil(W/8) design quarter-windows (W about 20, so 3 dropped); a premium carried by one reporting month is an episode, not a premium. (5) Regime: at least 3 of the 5 design years positive at the chosen cell. (6) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the fill spread as a share of the stop, the financing per trade and the number of fallback exits per arm are reported; if the chosen cell is positive gross but negative net, the lesson is that the premium is smaller than a weekly CFD round trip of about 0.15-0.25 percent of the index. (7) Replication on the difference, not on raw season R: the Director runs the matching ctrl cell of the chosen season cell once each on USA500IDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY (design and check only, horizon cut at the holdout start, scripts/run_backtest.py --end 2024-01-01, recorded in the cycle note as counted Director runs), and the pooled date-clustered season-minus-ctrl difference over the two markets (average the same-week difference across the two, then t over weeks) must be > 0 in design; the pooled-check and walk-forward hard gates on the season arm stand as written; JP225 uses jp_shift_days 14 so it tests the Tokyo reporting season rather than spill-over from the US one. (8) Pass bar: a positive result below the programme bar (design t >= 2 at the chosen cell with the design and check paired differences positive) is recorded as below the bar and is not promoted. Honest expectation: control 0 to +0.05 R in design, season 0 to +0.08 R above it; standard error of the difference about 0.14 R; P(design paired-D t >= 1 | effect real) about 0.25-0.35, about 0.16 if there is no effect; a kill is weak evidence; the most likely failure is that the premium, if any, sits on the announcement days and a five-day hold dilutes it below the weekly cost.

notes:
All times UTC. Bars: H1, stamped at the bar OPEN; sparse (whole hours are missing in 2013 and 2015-2017); locate every time by timestamp with F.first_bar_at_or_after and never assume one bar per hour.

WEEK SELECTION (calendar, UTC): mondays = unique F.utc_dates(m) with F.weekday == 0 and date >= np.datetime64(p['start']). For each Monday d: months = d.astype('datetime64[M]'); q0 = (months - (months.astype(np.int64) % 12 % 3).astype('timedelta64[M]')).astype('datetime64[D]') = the first day of the calendar quarter containing d; off = (d - q0).astype(int) in days (0..91). Unit check: 2015-02-16 gives q0 2015-01-01 and off 46; 2015-04-13 gives off 12. s0 = start_off + (jp_shift_days if m.sym starts with 'JPN' else 0). season(d) = s0 <= off < s0 + 7 * n_weeks. arm 'season' keeps Mondays with season(d) true; arm 'ctrl' keeps the others (every other week of the year); raise ValueError on any other arm value. US and Japanese holidays are not excluded; holiday Mondays that have a 15:00 UTC CFD bar are traded (expected).

ENTRY (decided from Monday information only): (eh, em) = F.parse_hhmm(p['entry_utc']) = 14:30; ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, eh, em), which is the 15:00 UTC bar on a normal Monday. Skip the week only if ei < 1, or ei >= m.n, or m.ts[ei] is more than max_delay_min (90) minutes after d 14:30 UTC, or ATR20[ei] is not finite or <= 0. No skip may depend on any bar after ei. sig = ei - 1 (the 14:00 bar); the fill is at the open of bar ei, i.e. 15:00 UTC = 11:00 New York in daylight time, 10:00 in winter (ask side plus slippage). entry_long[sig] = True; entry_type[sig] = 0; valid_bars[sig] = 1. Long only in both arms; the control arm measures the drift and cost that the season arm must beat.

STOP: daily = F.daily_bars(m); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, atr_n = 20)), known at the start of the trading day; read it at ei, not sig. sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[ei] (price units, > 0). tp_dist = NaN (no target). max_bars = 0.

EXIT: f = d + 4 days (the Friday of the same week); (xh, xm) = F.parse_hhmm(p['exit_utc']) = 19:30; xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, f, xh, xm), which is the 20:00 UTC bar on a normal Friday (the CFD session ends at 21:00 UTC in US daylight time, so the 20:00 bar is the last Friday bar then; the fill at its open is 16:00 New York in daylight time and 15:00 in winter). (a) Normal exit: if xi < m.n and xi > ei and m.ts[xi] is no more than max_exit_delay_min (180) minutes after f 19:30 UTC, set exit_long[xi - 1] = True (the 19:00 bar), closing at the open of bar xi. (b) Causal fallback: set exit_long[j] = True on every bar j with ts in [f 20:00 UTC, d + 7 days 12:00 UTC), i.e. Friday 20:00 to the following Monday 12:00, so a week whose Friday session is missing or cut short exits at the first bar after the gap instead of running into the next trade week; markers on bars with no open position are ignored by the executor. Never skip a week because of the Friday bars. No other exits, no filters, one trade per selected week; the executor blocks overlapping entries. Follow the causal pattern of strategies/auto/carry_cross_weekend_premium.py.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): arm (grid 'season', 'ctrl'), start_off (grid 10, 17), n_weeks (grid 4, 5), sl_atr (grid 1.0, 2.0); fixed entry_utc '14:30', exit_utc '19:30', max_delay_min 90, max_exit_delay_min 180, atr_n 20, start '2013-01-01', jp_shift_days 14 (added to start_off only when m.sym starts with 'JPN', because Tokyo companies with a March year-end report about two weeks after US large caps; no effect on the primary market). Module GRID = the full 16 cells so the checker exercises arm. Spec grids: stage A on USATECHIDXUSD runs all 16 cells (the 'ctrl' cells are control arms and run only there); stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run the season arm only (8 cells).

EXPECTED COUNTS (USATECHIDXUSD design 2013-2017, a check for the Builder and the checker): about 80 (n_weeks 4) or 100 (n_weeks 5) calendar season weeks before the few skips, about 70-90 after; control about 140-170. A count far below that means the week selection or the Friday exit is wrong. The Friday 20:00 UTC bar exists on 565 of 609 Fridays 2012-2023 on USATECHIDXUSD.

REPORTING (by the Director, from the trade lists of the chosen season cell and its matching ctrl cell, re-run with scripts/run_backtest.py --end 2024-01-01 --save-trades): per cell trades, avg R, t, season-window-clustered t (R averaged per calendar quarter of the entry date), mean fill spread in points and as a share of the stop, financing per trade in R (the engine charges 6 nights for a Monday-to-Friday hold because Wednesday is tripled), number of fallback (non-Friday-20:00) exits per arm, by-year avg R; the quarter-paired difference D_q (season mean minus non-season mean within each calendar quarter that has at least one week in each arm), its mean and t over quarters in design and in check; the same D with every week containing a scheduled FOMC decision dropped from both arms (dates from the 'Federal Funds Rate' rows of data/external/calendar_spoluan/forex_factory_calendar_YYYY.csv, which are stamped about 8 hours ahead of UTC, so '2014-01-30 03:00' is the 29 January 2014 decision); avg R and D by reporting season (January, April, July, October); the pooled date-clustered season-minus-ctrl difference over USA500IDXUSD and JPNIDXJPY.
